title: She is a jazz pianist before a composer
summary: She says piano comes first; arranging came from Kansas City and she lost records she had not copyrighted.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you consider yourself primarily a jazz pianist rather than a composer?

Yes, by all means. Jazz is my thing - I mean, piano is the thing but.......I gained merit from graces to write.) I didn't /Start to write until Kansas City. I told you about the scene where Andy and I used to sit all night taking down ideas, came back and I had them arranged. That was like a hobby with me then because I used to do it for practically nothing. I never made any money doing that nor have I ever been hired just as an arranger except when I traveled with Duke, oh 6 months in Canada and all around, when Harold Baker joined. No, I don't consider myself a composer-arranger. That's part of it but the basic thing is the piano because I can do so many things on the piano, switching and changing and doing things. I may not have the greatest technique but I can do things on piano that arranging and writing is secondary. My Arranging and composing comes while I'm playing piano. All the records I recorded
with Andy Kirk and didn't get paid for, I lost them all because I didn't have them copyrighted. I just sat down and played and my arranging and composing flows from playing.
